title: Exploring Substances: Acidic, Basic and Neutral
seo_title: Exploring Substances Class 7 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Curiosity Chapter 2)
standard_text: Acids, bases and neutral substances in daily life; natural and laboratory indicators such as litmus, turmeric and china rose; neutralisation and its uses in daily life: indigestion, ant bites, soil treatment and factory waste (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 2).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 7 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 2: acids, bases and neutral substances, litmus, turmeric and china rose indicators, and neutralisation in daily life. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Acids turn blue litmus red; bases turn red litmus blue.
body_html:
How to think about it

Acidic substances such as lemon juice, vinegar and curd taste sour; basic substances such as soap and baking soda feel soapy. Neutral substances such as sugar solution and distilled water are neither. We never taste unknown substances; we test them with indicators.

Acids turn blue litmus red and china rose dark pink; bases turn red litmus blue, turmeric red and china rose green. An acid and a base neutralise each other to form a salt and water, giving out heat. We use this for indigestion (antacids), ant stings (baking soda) and acidic soil (lime).

Example

Soap solution on turmeric paper?

soap is basic

Answer: it turns red

Example

Soil is too acidic. Add…

a base neutralises it

Answer: slaked lime or quicklime

Common mistakes

  • Thinking turmeric changes colour in acids.
  • Saying red litmus turns blue in acid.
  • Tasting a substance to test it.
